understanding: Drive modem handshake via modem_control_if with directed single-pin toggles plus simultaneous toggles plus MCR DTR/RTS/Out1/Out2 and loopback entry-exit coordinated with wishbone_bus MCR programming.
preconditions: Clock is stable at selected period and reset is released to inactive without assuming polarity per q_reset.
modem_control_if agent is active and owns cts_pad_i plus dsr_pad_i plus ri_pad_i plus dcd_pad_i drives and observes rts_pad_o plus dtr_pad_o plus inputs.
wishbone_bus agent is available for symbolic MCR programming of DTR plus RTS plus Out1 plus Out2 plus loopback without assuming address per q_bus.
DUT starts in normal operation with symbolic MCR loopback cleared per f_loop_mode.
stimulus_steps: FOR each pin in [cts_pad_i, dsr_pad_i, ri_pad_i, dcd_pad_i]: DRIVE single toggle to opposite level via modem_control_if; WAIT clock edge; SAMPLE monitor.
DRIVE constrained-random simultaneous toggles on a subset of inputs via modem_control_if; WAIT clock edge between interleavings; REPEAT with reproducible seed up to symbolic num_modem_events.
SET symbolic MCR loopback bit to 1 via wishbone_bus to enter loopback per f_loop_mode; WAIT clock edge.

WHILE in loopback: SET symbolic MCR DTR plus RTS plus Out1 plus Out2 via wishbone_bus per f_dtr_inv plus f_rts_inv plus f_out_map; OBSERVE routed equivalents via modem_control_if monitor without driving external inputs.
CLEAR symbolic MCR loopback bit to 0 via wishbone_bus to exit to normal per f_loop_mode; WAIT clock edge; RESUME external pin drives via modem_control_if.
IF external coordination needed: ORDER symbolic MCR programming on wishbone_bus before pin-drive bursts using events without virtual-interface delays.
check_steps: COMPARE observed rts_pad_o against inverted MCR RTS control per f_rts_inv on clock edges via modem_control_if monitor.
COMPARE observed dtr_pad_o against inverted MCR DTR control per f_dtr_inv on clock edges via modem_control_if monitor.
COMPARE loopback active state: STX_PAD_O is logic 1 and transmitter shift output is internally connected to receiver shift input per f_loop_mode.
COMPARE loopback routing DTR to DSR and RTS to CTS and Out1 to RI and Out2 to DCD per f_loop_map while loopback active.
SAMPLE modem_control_if monitor observations on clock edges for check activation; no driver-supplied expected results.
coverage_steps: SAMPLE cover for single-pin toggle on each of cts_pad_i and dsr_pad_i and ri_pad_i and dcd_pad_i.
SAMPLE cover for simultaneous-toggle combination with corner-biased multi-pin case.
SAMPLE cover for MCR DTR and RTS inversion values 0 and 1.
SAMPLE cover for loopback entry plus loopback-active with MCR controls plus loopback exit to normal.
completion: WAIT until all scheduled single toggles plus simultaneous toggles plus loopback entry-exit complete.
WAIT until modem_control_if monitor queue drains within TESTBENCH operational limit drain_cycles.
COMPARE all scheduled checks and FAIL on any mismatch; CLEANUP by clearing symbolic MCR loopback to normal and returning driven pins to idle level per q_idle.

facts.statement: DUT modem group comprises RTS_O, CTS_I, DTR_O, DSR_I, DCD_I and RI_I.
facts.quote:
RTS_O
CTS_I
DTR_O
DSR_I
DCD_I
RI_I

facts.statement: Six modem control signals are optional and may use general-purpose I/Os.
facts.quote:
and, optionally, another six modem
control signals, which can otherwise be implemented using general purpose I/Os on the
chip.

facts.statement: MCR bit0 controls DTR with 0 means pin 1 and 1 means pin 0.
facts.quote:
0 W Data Terminal Ready (DTR) signal control
 ‘0’ – DTR is ‘1’
 ‘1’ – DTR is ‘0’

facts.statement: MCR bit1 controls RTS with 0 means pin 1 and 1 means pin 0.
facts.quote:
1 W Request To Send (RTS) signal control
 ‘0’ – RTS is ‘1’
 ‘1’ – RTS is ‘0’

facts.statement: MCR Out1 connects to RI input and Out2 connects to DCD input in loopback mode.
facts.quote:
2 W Out1. In loopback mode, connected Ring Indicator (RI) signal input
3 W Out2. In loopback mode, connected to Data Carrier Detect (DCD)
input.

facts.statement: MCR bit4 0 is normal and 1 is loopback with STX_PAD_O set to 1 and TX shift internally to RX shift.
facts.quote:
4 W Loopback mode
 ‘0’ – normal operation
 ‘1’ – loopback mode. When in loopback mode, the Serial
Output Signal (STX_PAD_O) is set to logic ‘1’. The signal of the
transmitter shift register is internally connected to the input of the
receiver shift register.

facts.statement: Loopback makes DTR to DSR and RTS to CTS and Out1 to RI and Out2 to DCD.
facts.quote:
The following connections are made:
DTR Î  DSR
RTS Î CTS
Out1 Î RI
Out2 Î DCD

facts.statement: MCR bits 7-5 are ignored and MCR reset value is 0.

questions: q_idle: What are the inactive and idle driven levels for cts_pad_i, dsr_pad_i, ri_pad_i and dcd_pad_i? Do not infer from names.
q_reset: What is wb_rst_i active polarity and what are rts_pad_o and dtr_pad_o levels during reset and does MCR clear per f_mcr_reset?
q_bus: What are the WISHBONE pin addresses and byte lanes and write masks for MCR controls and for any MSR observation?
q_mcr_read: What does a WISHBONE read of write-only MCR return?
q_msr: What are the required MSR current-state versus delta semantics including complement versus loopback equality and DCTS plus DDSR plus TERI plus DDCD set and clear on read for checks?
q_ier: What IER enable combination gates modem-status interrupt observation during modem toggles?
q_timing: What setup plus hold and minimum spacing apply to modem input toggles relative to clock edges?
